sentences.text: Researchers evaluated a reliability-weighted planning algorithm across 1,800 runs in six deterministic 8x8 mazes featuring varying levels of model error.

While this method and a standard model-free approach achieved perfect success rates when only the planning model was corrupted, the reliability-aware method's success dropped to 60% on larger grids as corruption increased.
The model-free method's initial failure within a 200-episode limit was attributed by the authors to insufficient training time, as its success rate reached 100% at 1,000 episodes.

In environments with random action errors, the reliability-weighted method showed greater resilience to corruption but underperformed a fixed planning method when no corruption was present, while simplified intrinsic-exploration algorithms failed to solve a 16x16 maze within 200 episodes.
The authors present the connection to hippocampal replay as a computational analogy rather than a claim about actual neural mechanisms.
